Build a clean B2B SaaS frontend dashboard with configurable webhook integrations, professional UI, sidebar layout, jobs management, authentication, and no backend logic. see full details and instructions below : SOP – Frontend Web Interface for CV Analyzer SaaS
0. Golden Rules (READ FIRST – VERY IMPORTANT)
1.	Frontend only – no backend logic, no database access
2.	All business logic lives in n8n
3.	All data comes from webhooks
4.	Webhook URLs MUST be configurable
5.	Tenant isolation is handled by backend, not frontend
6.	Frontend must be stateless except for auth session
7.	No assumptions about database structure in frontend
________________________________________
1. Target Users & Usage Context
•	Primary user: Company Admin / HR Officer
•	Usage: Desktop-first (laptop), responsive for tablet
•	Environment: Secure internal business tool
•	Tone: Professional, calm, serious

2. Architecture & Tech Assumptions
2.1 Frontend Architecture
•	SPA (Single Page Application)
•	Framework: flexible (React / Vue / Svelte / Vanilla)
•	Routing: client-side
•	State:
o	Auth token
o	Current page
o	UI state only
2.2 Backend Interaction
•	HTTP webhooks (JSON)
•	Stateless requests
•	Authorization via token header

3. Configuration (MANDATORY)
3.1 Webhook URLs
All webhook URLs must be configurable via:
•	environment variables OR
•	config file OR
•	single config object
CONFIG = {
  LOGIN_WEBHOOK_URL,
  REGISTER_WEBHOOK_URL,
  GET_JOBS_WEBHOOK_URL,
  GET_JOB_DETAILS_WEBHOOK_URL,
  CREATE_JOB_WEBHOOK_URL,
  GET_APPLICATIONS_WEBHOOK_URL
}
🚫 Never hardcode URLs

4. Visual Design System (STRICT)
4.1 Design Style
•	B2B SaaS
•	Minimal
•	Flat (no heavy gradients)
•	Light mode only
4.2 Color Palette
Primary:        #2563EB
Primary Dark:   #1E40AF

Background:     #F8FAFC
Card:           #FFFFFF
Border:         #E5E7EB

Text Main:      #111827
Text Muted:     #6B7280

Success:        #16A34A
Warning:        #F59E0B
Error:          #DC2626
4.3 Typography
•	Font: Inter / Roboto / Open Sans
•	Page title: 20–24px
•	Section title: 16–18px
•	Body: 14–15px

5. Global Layout Rules
5.1 Unauthenticated Layout
•	Centered card
•	Max width: 480px
•	Tabs: Login | Register
•	Large primary button
•	Clear error messages
5.2 Authenticated Layout
Sidebar + Top Bar + Content
┌───────────────┬───────────────────────────────┐
│ Sidebar       │ Top Bar                        │
│ Jobs          │ Page Title                     │
│ Logout        │ Company / User Info            │
├───────────────┴───────────────────────────────┤
│ Main Content (tables / forms)                  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘

6. Authentication Flow
6.1 Login
Fields
•	Email
•	Password
Request
POST LOGIN_WEBHOOK_URL
{
  "email": "",
  "password": ""
}
Response (example)
{
  "success": true,
  "token": "...",
  "user": {
    "email": "",
    "role": "Admin",
    "tenant_name": ""
  }
}
Frontend behavior
•	Store token
•	Redirect to Jobs Dashboard

6.2 Registration
Fields
•	Company name
•	Admin full name
•	Admin email
•	Password
•	Confirm password
•	Inbox option:
o	Forward company email
o	Use system-generated email
•	If forwarding:
o	Company inbox email
Request
POST REGISTER_WEBHOOK_URL
{
  "company_name": "",
  "admin_name": "",
  "admin_email": "",
  "password": "",
  "intake_mode": "forwarding | generated",
  "forward_email": ""
}
Response
•	Success message
•	Generated inbox email (if applicable)

7. Jobs Dashboard
7.1 Jobs List
Loaded via:
GET GET_JOBS_WEBHOOK_URL
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Expected response (example)
[
  {
    "job_code": "",
    "job_title": "",
    "job_client": "",
    "job_status": "",
    "applications_total": 0,
    "applications_qualified": 0,
    "applications_partial": 0,
    "applications_rejected": 0
  }
]
7.2 Table UX Rules
•	Sticky header
•	Row hover highlight
•	Clickable links
•	Status badges
•	Empty state message

8. Job Details Page
Loaded via:
GET GET_JOB_DETAILS_WEBHOOK_URL?job_code=XXX
Display only – no editing
•	Use two-column layout on desktop
•	Stack on mobile

9. Add Job Flow
9.1 Add Job Button
•	Prominent
•	Primary color
•	Opens form (modal or page)
9.2 Job Form Fields
(Exactly as defined by backend)
Submit
POST CREATE_JOB_WEBHOOK_URL
Authorization: Bearer <token>
On success
•	Close form
•	Refresh jobs list
•	Show success toast

10. Applications Lists
Triggered by clicking counters.
Loaded via:
GET GET_APPLICATIONS_WEBHOOK_URL
?job_code=XXX
&filter=qualified|partial|rejected|all

11. UX & Interaction Rules (CRITICAL)
•	Show loading indicator on every webhook call
•	Disable submit buttons while loading
•	Never block UI without feedback
•	Errors must be shown as human-readable text
•	Use toast notifications for:
o	Success
o	Failure

12. Security Rules
•	Token stored securely
•	Token sent in Authorization header
•	Logout clears token and UI state
•	No token → redirect to login

13. Anti-Patterns (DO NOT DO)
🚫 Do NOT:
•	Hardcode tenant_id
•	Hardcode webhook URLs
•	Assume DB structure
•	Cache business data permanently
•	Perform validation beyond UI-level checks
•	Add AI logic to frontend

14. Acceptance Criteria
Frontend is accepted if:
•	User can register
•	User can login
•	Jobs list loads
•	Job details open
•	Job can be created
•	Applications can be listed
•	All actions go through webhooks
•	UI matches design system

**Defining Frontend Parameters**

I'm solidifying the core frontend requirements. React with TypeScript is the foundation, naturally. Tailwind CSS will ensure a clean, light-mode design with the specified color palette. Configuration of webhook URLs is a must-have for flexibility; no backend logic simplifies development but relies on webhook communication.


**Outlining the Components**

I've mapped out the essential visual structure: distinct layouts for unauthenticated and authenticated states. Key components are now clear: Login/Register forms, lists for jobs and applications, a job details view, and a form to add new jobs. I'm focusing on defining user interactions: loading states, button behaviors, and error handling with toast notifications. Token management is also underway, stored in state/session.

Context

The frontend login page already:

Sends credentials to the login webhook

Navigates to dashboard after submit

However, it does not yet handle the webhook response correctly, so users are allowed in even when credentials are wrong.

Backend behavior is already correct and must NOT be changed.

Objective

Update the frontend login logic so that navigation and login state depend strictly on the webhook response.

Required Behavior (Only What’s Missing)
1️⃣ Handle Login Response Properly

After calling the login webhook:

Read HTTP status code and response body

If response status is 401 / 403 OR response body contains:

{ "success": false }


Then:

Do NOT navigate

Do NOT store token

Show an error message returned by backend (or a generic one)

Only if response body contains:

{ "success": true, "token": "..." }


Then:

Store token

Store user object (if returned)

Navigate to dashboard

2️⃣ Login State Must Be Token-Based

User is considered logged in only if a valid token exists in storage

Navigation to dashboard must depend on presence of token

3️⃣ Error UX

Show error message clearly under login form

Keep user on login page

Disable login button while request is in progress

Re-enable button after response

4️⃣ Guard Protected Pages

On dashboard (and all internal pages):

On page load, check token existence

If token missing → redirect to login

This check must run on:

Page refresh

Direct URL access

5️⃣ Logout Handling

Logout must:

Remove stored token

Remove stored user info

Redirect to login page immediately

Acceptance Criteria

Wrong password → user stays on login page

Correct password → dashboard opens

Refresh dashboard → still logged in

Clear storage → dashboard redirects to login

Logout → session fully cleared

Constraints

Do NOT change backend

Do NOT assume login success

Do NOT auto-navigate without validating response

**Refining Authentication Logic**

I'm focusing on strengthening the authentication in the B2B SaaS frontend. The current login process feels a bit too forgiving, and I'm honing in on a more robust approach. I'm aiming to prevent accidental navigations on failure and better handle simulated scenarios.


**Implementing Strict Access Control**

I'm now prioritizing strict response handling to solidify authentication in the B2B SaaS frontend. I will ensure navigation only occurs with a successful response and valid token. I'll also incorporate specific error messages from the backend. The token-based authorization will be enforced for dashboard access. I also plan to add auth guards, redirecting to login on token absence. Lastly, I will implement a complete state and token clear on logout.


**Strengthening App Guards**

I'm now zeroing in on the SPA auth guard in `App.tsx`. The current check for `auth.token` seems solid. I will ensure the logout functionality in `Layout.tsx` thoroughly clears all state and token data. I'm also planning to review `Auth.tsx` to remove any unintended login simulations within the `handleLogin` function, ensuring it aligns with strict response validation. The `api.ts` checks are satisfactory.

<specification>
(i) what updates need to be made to the current app:
- Refine the authentication logic in `Auth.tsx` to strictly follow the webhook response.
- Remove automatic fallback/simulation in `Auth.tsx` that allowed unauthorized entry.
- Implement a local error display in the `AuthPage` for immediate feedback.
- Ensure the token is the single source of truth for the session.
- Verify the logout logic in `App.tsx` and `Layout.tsx` for complete state clearance.

(ii) the behaviour of the updates:
- **Login Flow**: Upon submission, the app waits for the webhook response. If `success` is `false` or the status code is error-level, it displays a descriptive error and remains on the login page.
- **Success Case**: Only when `success: true` and a `token` is present will the state be updated and the user navigated to the dashboard.
- **Auth Guard**: If a user attempts to access internal pages without a token (e.g., after clearing storage), they are automatically presented with the login view.
- **Logout**: Clicking logout resets the `auth` state to null and clears `localStorage`.

(iii) their visual appearance:
- A clear red error alert box will appear inside the auth card when authentication fails.
- Login/Register buttons will show a loading spinner and be disabled during requests.
- The UI remains professional and minimal, adhering to the B2B SaaS design system.
</specification>

We have a working React/TypeScript frontend for “CV Analyzer”. Currently, after login it always redirects to the tenant Job Dashboard (tenant-scoped).
Now we added a Super Admin (system admin) role and a set of super admin APIs in n8n. Update the frontend to differentiate super_admin vs other roles with minimal changes.

1) Auth + role source

The JWT payload includes role (example: super_admin or admin).

We already have an auth guard backend workflow that validates the JWT and returns:

Auth verify response shape:

{
  "user": {
    "sub": "user_id",
    "tenant_id": "tenant_uuid",
    "email": "email",
    "role": "super_admin",
    "iat": 1234567890
  }
}


Frontend must store:

token

user.role

user.tenant_id

⚠️ Roles in DB may be mixed case (Admin, admin, super_admin). Treat role check as:

role.toLowerCase() === 'super_admin'

2) Routing behavior change (main requirement)

After successful login:

If role is super_admin → redirect to Super Admin Dashboard route: /super-admin

Else → keep existing behavior → redirect to existing Jobs Dashboard route (current default) e.g. /jobs (or your current route)

Also protect routes:

/super-admin/* must be accessible ONLY for super_admin.

tenant pages (jobs/applications/job-details) remain as they are.

3) New Super Admin pages (minimal UI)

Create a new section/layout:

Left sidebar item “Super Admin” only visible for super_admin

New page: Super Admin Dashboard /super-admin

Tabs inside it (or subpages):

Tenants /super-admin/tenants

Users /super-admin/users

Keep styling consistent with existing app (same layout/colors/components).

4) Backend base URL / endpoints

Backend is n8n webhooks under:

https://n8n.ai970.cloud/webhook

4.1 Super Admin Dashboard (overview + tenants list)

GET:
/cv-saas/admin/dashboard
Full URL:
https://n8n.ai970.cloud/webhook/cv-saas/admin/dashboard

Response:

{
  "overview": {
    "total_tenants": 0,
    "active_tenants": 0,
    "total_users": 0,
    "total_jobs": 0,
    "total_applications": 0,
    "applications_today": 0,
    "failed_ingest_24h": 0
  },
  "tenants": [
    {
      "tenant_id": "uuid",
      "tenant_name": "name",
      "tenant_code": "code",
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "iso",
      "users_count": 0,
      "jobs_count": 0,
      "applications_count": 0
    }
  ]
}

4.2 Tenants paginated list

GET:
/cv-saas/admin/tenants?page=1&limit=10&search=BA

Response:

{
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 10,
  "total": 5,
  "total_pages": 1,
  "tenants": [ ...same tenant object as above... ]
}

4.3 Users global list (paginated + filters)

GET:
/cv-saas/admin/users?page=1&limit=10&search=&tenant=&role=&status=

Response:

{
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 10,
  "total": 11,
  "total_pages": 2,
  "users": [
    {
      "user_id": "uuid",
      "email": "x",
      "full_name": "x",
      "role": "admin",
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "iso",
      "last_login_at": null,
      "tenant_id": "uuid",
      "tenant_name": "x",
      "tenant_code": "x"
    }
  ]
}

4.4 Update user status

PATCH:
/cv-saas/admin/users/status
Body:

{ "user_id": "uuid", "status": "active" }


or

{ "user_id": "uuid", "status": "disabled" }


Response:

{ "success": true, "user": { ...updated user... } }

4.5 Update tenant status (with cascade disable users)

PATCH:
/cv-saas/admin/tenants/status
Body:

{ "tenant_id": "uuid", "status": "active" }


or

{ "tenant_id": "uuid", "status": "suspended" }


Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "tenant": { ...updated tenant... },
  "users_disabled_count": 0
}

5) Authorization header

All these endpoints require:
Authorization: Bearer <token>

If backend returns:

{ "error": "Missing Authorization header", "statusCode": 401 }


Frontend must redirect to login and clear token.

If 403 access denied → show “Access denied”.

6) UI requirements (simple)
Super Admin Dashboard page:

Show overview cards using overview numbers.

Show a table of tenants from dashboard.tenants (or call /admin/tenants).

Each tenant row: name, code, status badge, users/jobs/applications counts, created_at.

Add “Suspend/Activate” button per tenant calling PATCH tenant status.

Super Admin Users page:

Table of users with columns: email, full_name, role, status badge, tenant_name, created_at, last_login_at.

Filters: search (email/name), tenant (name/code), role, status, plus pagination.

Add “Disable/Activate” button calling PATCH user status.

7) Minimal code changes rule

Do NOT refactor the whole app.

Reuse existing api service and auth state patterns.

Add new routes + pages + navigation conditionally.

Implement these changes now.

**Defining Super Admin Access**

I'm currently focused on defining the implementation for a Super Admin role within the React/TypeScript dashboard. My initial thought is that a case-insensitive check for the `super_admin` role must be implemented. Also, the existing authentication payload, which includes the user's `sub`, `tenant_id`, `email`, `role`, and `iat`, and that the `token` and `user` object will be stored, will be used.

I'm focusing on GET requests for overviews, paginated lists, and PATCH requests for status updates, all requiring bearer token authorization. I'll conditionally show the "Super Admin" links in the sidebar, and I have plans to update config and type files. I'll have to update app routing also.

I'm updating `App.tsx` for proper view switching, specifically after login based on the user's role. I've also added conditional logic to the layout to display the admin navigation based on the user's role. Finally, I've created the `AdminDashboard.tsx` and `AdminUsers.tsx` pages.
